name: Luck
description: Chance, Coincidence, The Break That Goes Your Way. Where Fortune is destiny at the scale of empires, Luck is the small stuff: the loose stone that holds, the guard who looks the other way, the arrow that goes wide by a finger's width. It cannot be relied on, which is the entire point — and its wielders spend their lives learning exactly how much of it they can get away with.

cost.text: Pressing It. Each time you draw a second or later Luck seal before you finish a long rest, roll a d6. On a 1, the luck turns: the next d20 you roll before your next turn is made at disadvantage, and someone nearby notices how long your streak was.
cost.card: PRESSING IT — 2nd+ Luck seal in a day: d6, on a 1 your next d20 is at disadvantage

minor.name: Off-stride
minor.card: disadvantage on its next attack roll

major.name: Cursed footing
major.card: Prone, and its next save is at disadvantage

severe.name: Nothing goes right
severe.card: Incapacitated as everything it tries fails at once

offensive.name: The Break
offensive.description: Nothing about this should have hit. It hit.

tiers.text: The damage becomes force. If the seal's attack roll or the target's save came within 2 of the number needed, it deals 2 additional dice — the margin was luck, and luck is yours.
tiers.card: Damage becomes Force · +2 dice when the roll was within 2 either way

tiers.text: Reroll any damage dice that come up 1 or 2, once.
tiers.card: Reroll the 1s and 2s once

tiers.text: The seal scores a critical hit on a 19 or 20 — and on a save, a natural 1 from the target counts as failing by 10 for anything that cares how badly it failed.
tiers.card: Crits on 19–20 · their natural 1 counts as failing by 10

tiers.text: Absurd. Something ridiculous happens in your favour: the DM names a coincidence that costs the target its reaction, its footing, its weapon or its cover — and it was going to happen anyway.
tiers.card: ABSURD — a coincidence costs them their reaction, footing, weapon or cover

supportive.name: Riding It
supportive.description: For the next little while, things simply go their way.

tiers.text: For 1 minute the target may roll a d4 once and add it to any attack roll, ability check or saving throw, after seeing the result.
tiers.card: 1 min: once, +1d4 to any d20 — after seeing the roll

tiers.text: The die becomes a d6, and the target may use it twice. The first time it rolls a natural 1 while this lasts, treat the roll as a 10 instead.
tiers.card: d6, twice · the first natural 1 becomes a 10

tiers.text: Once while this lasts, the target may turn a hit against it into a miss, or a failed saving throw into a success. Nobody will be able to say quite how.
tiers.card: Once: a hit becomes a miss, or a failed save becomes a success

tiers.text: Golden. The die becomes a d8 and may be used any number of times, the target's critical hits land on 19 or 20, and the first time each round it would suffer a random effect, you choose the result instead.
tiers.card: GOLDEN — +1d8 at will · crits on 19–20 · you choose any random result against it, 1/round

control.name: The Streak Ends
control.description: You take the small mercies away and let the odds do the work.

tiers.text: A creature that fails loses its luck: it can't gain advantage from any source until the end of its next turn, and rerolls no dice.
tiers.card: Fail: no advantage from any source, no rerolls, until the end of their next turn

tiers.text: A creature that fails scores a critical hit only on a natural 20 that it then confirms with a second attack roll, and treats its natural 20s on saving throws as ordinary successes.
tiers.card: Their crits need confirming · their nat 20s on saves are just successes

tiers.text: The effect lasts 1 minute, repeating the save at the end of each of its turns, and while it holds the creature suffers a complication each round: the DM names something small that goes wrong — a strap, a footing, a torch, a spooked horse.
tiers.card: 1 min (Cha save each turn) · something small goes wrong for them each round

conditions.name: Luckless
conditions.escape: Charisma save at the end of each of its turns

tiers.text: The Long Odds. While the effect holds, any natural 1 the creature rolls is a catastrophe of the DM's design, and any ally who lends it advantage, a reroll, or a shared bonus must succeed on the save or lose that ability until the effect ends.
tiers.card: THE LONG ODDS — their natural 1s become catastrophes · helping them costs the helper too

utility.name: Happenstance
utility.description: You ask the world for a small favour, and it is usually in a good mood.

tiers.text: Find something small you need but did not pack — a coin, a candle, a key that fits well enough, the right name to drop — as long as it could plausibly be nearby.
tiers.card: Find the small thing you needed but didn't pack

tiers.text: Arrive at the right moment: once per day, declare that you turned up exactly when something was about to happen, and you did.
tiers.card: 1/day: you arrived exactly when it mattered, and you did

tiers.text: Nudge a coincidence for 8 hours: a guard is drunk, a ship is delayed, a door was left unbarred, a rival is out of town. Nothing that directly harms anyone.
tiers.card: Nudge a coincidence for 8 hrs — a lax guard, a late ship, an open door

tiers.text: Spend a piece of it: once per long rest, an event of the DM's design that would have gone badly for you goes well instead, and someone else's luck is quietly worse for it.
tiers.card: 1/long rest: a bad event turns good — and somebody else pays for it

creation.name: Charms
creation.description: Things you make have a habit of being exactly where they are wanted.

tiers.text: Your creations turn up conveniently: each is found, placed or positioned exactly where it is most useful within its range.
tiers.card: Creations land exactly where they'd be most useful

tiers.text: Your Objects are charms — whoever carries one may reroll one d20 per day.
tiers.card: Objects are charms: one reroll a day for whoever carries them

tiers.text: Your Structures are never quite hit: the first attack or effect that would damage one each round misses or fizzles.
tiers.card: 1/round, the first hit on a Structure simply misses

tiers.text: Make a Talisman: a permanent Object that gives its bearer one reroll per short rest, and cannot be lost — when misplaced, it turns up again within a day, usually somewhere absurd.
tiers.card: A TALISMAN — a reroll per short rest, and it always comes back

complementEffects.name: Fluke
complementEffects.description: Something went right that had no business going right.

effect.text: On a hit or failed saving throw, the target takes bonus force damage equal to one damage die of the primary effect's type (min 1d6). If the seal's roll succeeded by 2 or less, roll that die twice.
effect.card: +1 die force — twice if the roll succeeded by 2 or less

upgrades.text: Level 5+: Two dice, and you may reroll any 1s on the seal's damage.
Level 11+: Three dice, and the seal crits on a 19 as well as a 20.

complementEffects.name: Fair Winds
complementEffects.description: Everything is about to go slightly better for everyone the seal touched.

effect.text: Each of the seal's targets may roll a d4 once before the end of your next turn and add it to one attack roll, check or saving throw, after seeing the result.
effect.card: The seal's targets: +1d4 once, after seeing the roll

upgrades.text: Level 5+: The die becomes a d6 and lasts 1 minute.
Level 11+: Each target's first natural 1 while it lasts is treated as a 10.

complementEffects.name: Bad Break
complementEffects.description: The seal lands, and then their footing goes.

effect.text: A creature hit by or failing the seal can't gain advantage from any source until the end of its next turn.
effect.card: No advantage from any source until the end of their next turn

upgrades.text: Level 5+: It also can't reroll any die until then.
Level 11+: The next attack roll made against it has advantage, as something gives way underfoot.
upgrades.card: The next attack on them has advantage
